findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser record
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil (for example a logged-in user who opens or is forwarded an unsubscribe link for a topic they have never visited/interacted with, so no topic_users row exists). Lines 107-113 unconditionally call tu.notification_level and tu.save!, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of unsubscribing. Use TopicUser.change (which creates the row) or guard/create the record before updating.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe is exposed as an unauthenticated-token GET request
findings.body: The unsubscribe action mutates notification_level on a plain GET, requires only the ambient login cookie (ensure_logged_in) and skips check_xhr. Any cross-site page can force a logged-in victim's browser to request /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe (e.g. via an tag) and downgrade/mute arbitrary topics for that victim without CSRF protection or a per-user/per-topic signed token. Email unsubscribe links should carry an unguessable token, or require a confirmation POST.

findings.title: Unsubscribe action is not idempotent and progressively mutes the topic
findings.body: If notification_level is above regular it is set to regular, otherwise it is set to muted. Re-opening the same email link, refreshing the landing page, or a mail scanner/prefetcher hitting the link a second time therefore takes a user who already unsubscribed (regular) and mutes the topic, which also removes it from topic lists — a stronger effect than requested. Repeated hits should converge on one terminal level (regular), not toggle downwards on each GET.

findings.title: Unsubscribe template path does not match the topicUnsubscribe route
findings.body: The Ember route is the top-level route 'topicUnsubscribe' (app-route-map.js.es6 line 13, routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6, controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6, views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6), whose template name resolves to 'topic-unsubscribe'. The template is instead placed at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which registers as 'topic/unsubscribe' (a nested topic route that does not exist). The unsubscribe page will therefore render with a missing/empty template and the notification dropdown in this file will not be shown.

findings.title: Direct TopicUser save bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping
findings.body: Setting notification_level directly and calling save! bypasses TopicUser.change, which is the codebase path that stamps notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, runs observe_after_save callbacks and publishes the /topic/:id MessageBus notification_level_change. Clients already viewing the topic and derived tracking state can therefore keep showing the old watching/tracking level after an unsubscribe until a reload, and the change is not recorded with a reason/time.

findings.title: Global unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url for every email that uses it
findings.body: unsubscribe_link is interpolated by Email::MessageBuilder for any mail built with add_unsubscribe_link: true (body and html_part), using template_args merged from the caller's opts. The new template unconditionally references %{unsubscribe_url}, but only UserNotifications#send_notification_email supplies unsubscribe_url; any other current/future caller with add_unsubscribe_link and no unsubscribe_url will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument (or render a broken link) when building the email. The per-topic sentence should be conditional or a default unsubscribe_url should be provided, and no new spec covers the unsubscribe controller action or an email built without unsubscribe_url.
